texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report arises out of road accident that occurred on 25.12.2021, in which one Rahul Popli(aged about 26 years) allegedly suffered grievous injury. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 25.12.2021, on receipt of DD no.113A, HC Ramavtar reached at spot i.e. Pocket 8A, Kalkaji Ext where public handed over the custody of one injured to police and came to know that other injured had been taken to unknown hospital. On 31.12.2021, relative of the injured came to police station and informed that injured Rahul is under treatment in AIIMS Trauma Center. On 01.01.2022, one eye witness Gulshan Kumar came to the police station and told about the accident. He told that on 22.12.2021, son of his maternal uncle namely Rahul Popli came to meet him and on 25.12.2021 at about 9.30 PM, he and injured Rahul Popli were strolling outside their house and going towards Pocket 8 from Pocket A-3, suddenly one motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SE-3448(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) Splender black colour hit injured Rahul Popli. Due to such impact injured as well as rider of motorcycle received injuries. He took victim/injured Rahul Popli to Majidia hospital where doctor referred him for Trauma Center where his treatment was going on. MLC No.500296424/2022 was obtained in which injuries were mentioned as "Grievous". 3. An FIR no.0003/22, dated 01.01.2022 was registered u/s CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.11.24 17:35:53 +0530 MACT No.607/24 Rahul @Rahul Popli v. Arshad P.No. 2 Of 23 BK 279,337 of IPC, PS Govindpuri, Distt-South East. Matter was investigated. During investigation, it was found that driver of motorcycle was not holding Driving Licence. A chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court u/s 279/338 IPC and 3/181,5/180 MV Act against driver of the offending vehicle while the present DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. As per record, Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent no.3 is insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Respondent no.1/Driver filed his reply submitting that injured was under the influence of liquor and crossing the road with faltering steps and suddenly in front of motorcycle. That the offending vehicle was insured on the date of accident. Respondent no.2/owner did not file any reply. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed its reply in Form-III and submitted that FIR was lodged on 01.01.2022 as there is an unexplained delay of one week. Driver of offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident. However, it admitted that the offending vehicle was insured on the date of accident. 6. On the basis of pleadings on record, following issues were framed on 22.07.2024. Rahul @Rahul Popli (Dar) vs Arshad@Aryan (03/22 Gp) on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164703410/ 2 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 25.12.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-3SEJ-3448 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.11.24 17:35:59 +0530 MACT No.607/24 Rahul @Rahul Popli v. Arshad P.No. 3 Of 23 BK whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/injured examined himself as PW-1. To prove his claim, petitioner /Rahul led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the DAR. He stated that on 25.12.2021 at about 9.30 PM, after having dinner, he was going for a walk from Pocket A-3 to Pocket-8. Suddenly a motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SE-J-3448 came at high speed rashly and negligently and hit him. Due to such impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and admitted to AIIMS hospital. He was admitted on 27.12.2021 and discharged on 01.01.2022. He was diagnosed with "BB Leg Rt open Grade I with Fibrous, non-union Medical Malleolus" and underwent a surgery "Crif with Suprapatellar Nailing Rt+ Orif with CCS For Medical Malleolus Rt under CSE"on 28.12.2021. He spent Rs.29,553/- for his treatment, Rs.1,00,000/- on special diet and conveyance. He suffered 34% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb issued by Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya hospital. He was working in private company and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m. He is MBA Post graduate. PW-1 relied upon MLC of JPN Apex Trauma Center as Ex.PW-1/1, AIIMS hospital discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/2, Medical bills as Mark A to E, Medical bills inovice T-777/21-22 as Ex.PW-1/3, DAR as Ex.PW-1/4, Disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/5, educational certificate as Ex.PW-1/6, Aadhar card as CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.11.24 17:36:04 +0530 MACT No.607/24 Rahul @Rahul Popli v. Arshad P.No. 4 Of 23 BK Mark-F and PAN Card as Ex.PW-1/8. PW-1 as duly cross examined by counsel for driver and insurance company. Respondent no.1 led his evidence by examined Sh. Arshad as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R-1W-1/A. He deposed that he has falsely been implicated in the present matter. That on the date of accident, he was not driving the vehicle in question and the FIR has been registered after delay of six days. He relied upon the reply dated 19.03.2025 filed by Addl. CP South-East as Mark-A. He was cross - examined by learned counsel for petitioner and insurance company. Insurance company/Respondent no.3 examined Sh. Akhalya RD, Claim Service Manager-Ckaims, Legal, TATA AIG General Insurance Company Ltd. as R-3W-1. He tendered his evidence by way of Rahul @Rahul Popli (Dar) vs Arshad@Aryan (03/22 Gp) on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164703410/ 3 affidavit as Ex.R-3W-1/A. He relied upon the the authority letter as Ex.R-3W-1/B. He deposed that the offending vehicle was insured in the name of one Sukhveer Singh from 28.07.2019 to 27.07.2024 vide policy no.3190292351. Same is Ex.R-3W-1/C. Driver of the offending vehicle was driving the offending vehicle without driving licence on the date of accident, hence they are not liable to pay the compensation to the victim. Legal notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC is Ex.R-2W-1/D. He was cross-examined by counsel for Respondent no.1. 8. 10. In the present case, petitioner has testified as PW-1 to allege that factum and manner of accident. He has categorically alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven in a rash and negligent manner. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents. Insurance company/respondent no.3 has raised statutory defence that the Respondents were in violation of the terms of the policy in as much as Respondent no.1 did not have a valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle. In order to prove this defence, insurance company has examined Sh. Akhalya RD, Claims Service Manager, Legal as R-3W-1 who has proved service of Notice u/O 12 Rule 8 CPC to the driver and owner of offending vehicle alongwith its receipts as Ex.R3W1/D. As such , Respondent no.1 and 2 are held to have been in breach of the terms of insurance policy and thus liable to compensate the petitioner.

The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
